thread:
Sarah: idea — add an ephemeral 'sudo' session flow in the console for tenant admins so they can take temporary elevated actions without modifying role bindings permanently
Josh: product likes it, less role churn for ad-hoc tasks :thumbsup:
Mina: main concerns: audit trail, telemetry tagging, and quota semantics. we need an audit_id attached to every request and a clear authz contract
Sarah: constraints I'm thinking about:
- default TTL 15m, configurable by enterprise policy up to 2h
- MFA enforced for sessions >30m
- console banner: "You are acting as: <scope> (temporary)"
- every request during a sudo session must set audit_id and sudo=true in auth metadata
Keven: UX ask: confirmation modal listing allowed actions + one-click Revoke button
Mina: telemetry notes: mark traces/events with sudo=true and attach audit_id. make sure sampling still surfaces sudo sessions in error traces (even if low-rate)
Sarah: example create call (API draft):
```
POST /admin/v1/ephemeral_sessions
{
  "actor": "sarah",
  "target_scope": "org:billing:write",
  "ttl_seconds": 900,
  "mfa_verified": true
}
=> 201
{
  "ephemeral_token": "ek-***",
  "audit_id": "sesh_2026_0001",
  "expires_at": "2026-09-29T12:34:56Z"
}
```
Josh: product asks the console's effective-permissions preview should reflect the ephemeral scope so admins see exactly what they can do live
Mina: authz service: we need a fast-path to validate ephemeral tokens and emit audit tuples. possible reuse of sidecar auth cache but protect against spike storms
Keven: quotas question — should sudo sessions bypass per-user soft limits? I think we should calculate quota/rate by the effective principal (the elevated scope) to avoid surprising behavior
Sarah: agreed. routing should use effective principal for quota and affinity. add header X-Effective-Principal: <resolved-principal> so downstream systems know it's an ephemeral elevation
Mina: telemetry/invoicing: label ephemeral usage separately in token-level cost/latency breakdowns so enterprise invoices can show ephemeral-bucketed usage
infra-bot: deployment note — backend API + audit sink must land before UI. adding feature flag: console.ephemeral_sudo
Josh: rollout plan suggestion:
1) internal alpha (eng + SE)
2) opt-in enterprise beta
3) automatic for tenants with enterprise policy enabled
Keven: edge cases: block service accounts from interactive sudo unless explicitly allowed; prevent cloning of ephemeral sessions for automation use-cases
Mina: security: keep full request context for 90 days, store audit_id in immutable audit logs; expose revoke endpoint:
```
POST /admin/v1/ephemeral_sessions/{audit_id}/revoke
```
Sarah: UI copy ideas: "You are operating temporarily as <scope>. Actions are audited and will expire at <time>." CTA: "End session"
Josh: analytics asks: add counters ephemeral.session.started and ephemeral.session.revoked with tenant_id and initiated_by_id tags
Mina: performance target: ephemeral authz check should add <2ms median. if slower, cache validated decisions for TTL but force fresh check on high-sensitivity actions (billing, role changes, revoke)
Keven: canary approach: 10% orgs, monitor audit sink QPS, sudo-tagged traces/errors, and quota anomalies. Add sampling ramp guard on routing to avoid authz avalanches
Sarah: next steps:
- Mina + infra: spec API + audit sink schema
- Keven + infra: routing header + quota semantics doc
- Josh + design: modal copy + effective-permissions preview changes
- Sarah: draft canary playbook
Mina: I'll produce an API PR with telemetry mappings today and tag Josh for review
Josh: I'll update the console release checklist and product notes
Keven: I'll add the feature flag and a sampling protection in routing to throttle authz lookups during spikes
Sarah: thanks everyone. if no objections I'll file a short RFC on eng-platform tomorrow :eyes:
Josh: no objections from product
Mina: none from security
infra-bot: feature-flag created: console.ephemeral_sudo (owner: keven)
